Healthcare providers generally do not receive adequate education on how to properly use metered-dose inhalers (MDIs). This is evident in the retrieved matches, where multiple sub-questions are raised about this topic. 

A study confirmed that a significant percentage of patients misuse MDIs and does not follow proper guidelines for its use. Furthermore, healthcare providers lack understanding of the proper usage, with one match stating that it supports the use of respiratory care practitioners in outpatient settings when they are proficient in using MDIs.

In terms of education, family physicians in British Columbia have limited awareness of the costs associated with medical care, as highlighted in another match. Target Serum Urate and Gout patients also show a knowledge deficit regarding their treatment goals, emphasizing the need for better education on these topics.

Regarding inhaled steroids and cromones for asthma management, some studies suggest that MDIs are more effective than cromones in preventing hospital admissions for asthma in children when administered correctly. However, counter sampling combined with medical provider education may not have a significant impact on prescribing behavior, as noted in another match.
